subject: Dedicated capacity onboarding: orchestration mapping, SLA asks, and regional constraints
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Maya Chen <maya@edgescale.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -0000
Subject: Dedicated capacity onboarding: orchestration mapping, SLA asks, and regional constraints

Hi Maya —

Thanks for choosing Redwood Dedicated. I’m Olga from Customer Success and I’ll lead the onboarding for EdgeScale’s GPU pool. Attached is a short SOW draft and a regional-capacity matrix to capture constraints (edge-implementation-sow.pdf; regional-capacity-matrix.xlsx).

Before our kickoff call, can you confirm the following so we can size the pool and propose autoscale/burst settings?

- Expected steady-state QPS / requests-per-second and peak QPS (weekday peak and launch-day surge).
- Typical concurrent sessions and p95 response-time SLO (token-length assumptions if available).
- Preferred primary region(s) and any hard data-residency requirements (EU / APAC constraints).
- Tolerance for transient failures and acceptable fallback (e.g., fallback to a smaller model variant).
- Any procurement or firewall/VPN contacts we should loop in for netops work.

High-level thoughts from our side (we’ll confirm with Ops after we have the numbers):
- Suggest a warm pool of 2 nodes per region + autoscale to handle sustained increases.
- Burst policy can be time-boxed and capped per-day to control costs; we’ll propose an initial cap based on your peak QPS.
- We recommend H100 80GB for lower-latency generative workloads, A100 if you need a more cost-friendly option.

Propose a 45-minute kickoff tomorrow or Thursday to walk the matrix and confirm owners. Let me know which time suits you.

Thanks — looking forward.

Best,
Olga Petrov

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity onboarding: orchestration mapping, SLA asks, and regional constraints

Hi Olga —

Thanks for the note — excited to get this moving. Quick answers below:

- Steady-state: ~180 QPS across inference endpoints (averaged), peak: 1,200 QPS for 2–3 hours during batch jobs / marketing launches.
- Concurrent sessions: typically 80–120 active user sessions; p95 latency target for API is 500ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens), up to 1.5s for longer generation (<=1,024 tokens).
- Regions: Primary in US (west) and EU (Ireland); APAC (Singapore) required for a small subset of traffic (~10%) due to latency-sensitive customers.
- Data residency: EU customer subset must not leave region for inference (data-at-rest in region + KMS control).
- Procurement/NetOps: cc’d is our infra lead (I’ll loop them separately after initial sizing).

We can support a kickoff Thu 2026-09-10 17:00 UTC. I’ve attached a small traffic sample and a short runbook excerpt for token distributions — traffic-trace-sample.zip.

Maya

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Maya Chen <maya@edgescale.io>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 14:30:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity onboarding: orchestration mapping, SLA asks, and regional constraints

Maya / Olga —

Thanks for the traffic sketch — that’s helpful. Operational notes and a provisional pool sizing below. This is preliminary until we see the full token-length distribution and regional split from the trace.

Provisional topology (per-region):
- Machine class: recommend H100-80GB for primary clusters (lower tail latency) with A100 as a fallback/secondary cluster for cost-sensitive workloads.
- Warm pool: 2 nodes (per region) to cover cold-starts for small bursts.
- Baseline capacity: US-west 3 nodes, EU-ireland 2 nodes, APAC-sg 1 node (initial).
- Autoscale policy: scale-up aggressively on queue length with target-concurrency-based decisions. Suggested policy:
  * Min: warm pool size (2)
  * Desired: baseline capacity above (3/2/1)
  * Sustained target: 6 nodes (global aggregate) for typical launch windows
  * Burst cap: 12 nodes global (time-boxed, 12 hrs/day cap during marketing runs)

Questions for EdgeScale:
- Confirm expected percent of peak that is long-generation (>512 tokens) vs short (<256 tokens). Long generations drive KV cache and memory pressure; affects whether H100 is mandatory for parts of the fleet.
- Confirm if you want cross-region bursting (i.e., surge in US can allocate spare capacity in EU) or strictly regional boundaries due to residency.

NetOps / firewall requests we’ll need (work to be scheduled by NetOps):
- Provide static egress IP ranges for us to white-list and a list of ingress VIPs we should advertise.
- If using private VPC peering, we’ll need contact for transient peering windows and expected CIDR ranges.

I’ll prepare a short MOP (method of procedure) draft and a candidate autoscale JSON to attach to the kickoff agenda. Olga — I’ll also add a quick cost delta table comparing H100 vs A100 for the proposed burst scenarios.

-ben
Ben Carter
Principal Reliability Engineer, Dedicated Capacity
ben@redwood.com
